text: The best way to learn a new skill is to notice what happens while you practice. A short session can reveal a pattern that a long session hides. Perhaps a familiar word feels easy, while a common pair of letters slows you down. That observation is useful because it points to a specific next step. You can work on that step, take a break, and return with fresh attention. Speed matters, but accuracy gives speed a strong foundation. When the two grow together, the work starts to feel lighter. This is true at a keyboard, in a workshop, or on a running path. Results are most helpful when they explain where you are today and make the next attempt easier to choose. They do not need to define your ability forever. Keep the goal small enough to repeat. Measure it honestly, then give yourself room to improve.
